summary: Krishna Kanta Handiqui (1898–1982) was an Indologist. He studied at Cotton University, Sanskrit College and University, Calcutta, Oxford, Paris, and Berlin. He served as Principal of Jagannath Barooah College (1930–1948) and Vice-Chancellor of Gauhati University (1948–1957).

Krishna Mohan Banerjee (1813–1885) was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar. Educated at Hare School, Presidency College, under Alexander Duff, and at Bishop's College, he later served at Hare School (~1828–1831) and as Second Professor at Bishop's College (1852).

Krishna Venkateswara Sarma (1919–2005) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. Educated at University College Thiruvananthapuram and University of Kerala under V. A. Ramaswami Sastri, he held posts at Kerala, University of Madras, Panjab University, VVRI, and Adyar Library.

Krishnanath Chatterjee was a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Surendra Nath Bhattacharya, Haripada Chakravarty, Ramaranjan Mukherji, Krishna Gopal Goswami, Satkari Mookerjee, Amarasvar Thakur, and Siddheswar Bhattacharya.
Kristen De Joseph is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She studied under Arlo Griffiths and is a PhD candidate at Leiden University under doctoral supervisor Peter Bisschop (attested 2026).

Kristin Johnston Largen is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. In 2018, she was attested as Professor of Systematic Theology at United Lutheran Seminary and Associate Dean of Religious and Spiritual Life at Gettysburg College.

Kristin Scheible works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied at Colby College and Harvard under Anne E. Monius, Diana L. Eck, John S. Strong, and Charles Hallisey. She has held posts at Harvard, Brown, and Bard College.

Kristina Myrvold is an Indology and religious studies scholar who was a Ph.D. candidate and editor at Lund University. By 2014, she held a post as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Linnaeus University.

Kristofer Schipper (1934–2021) was a sinologist and religious studies scholar who studied in Paris and at Academia Sinica. He held appointments at EFEO, EPHE, CNRS, Collège de France, and Leiden University.

Krisztina Teleki (born 1978) is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She completed her MA at Eötvös Loránd University (~1996–2009), where she also served as a research fellow (~2009).
Kshanika Saha is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied under Nalinaksha Dutt and earned a PhD from the University of Calcutta (attested 1966).

Kshetreśachandra Chattopadhyaya (1896–1974) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. Educated at Calcutta, Presidency College, Allahabad, and Sampurnanand under Ganganatha Jha, he served as a lecturer, reader, and professor at Allahabad, and as Director of Sampurnanand's Research Institute.

Kshitimohan Sen (1880–1960) was a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. Educated at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, he served in the Chamba State Education Department (~1904–1908), at Patha Bhavana, and as Adhyaksha at Visva-Bharati University (1953–1954).

K. L. Dhammajoti (born 1949) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Yinshun and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa at the University of Kelaniya. He held posts at Kelaniya, University of Calgary, Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and University of Hong Kong.

Kumataro Kawada (1899–1981) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. Educated at the University of Tokyo, he held teaching posts at Japan Women's University (1927), Tokyo University of Literature and Science (1943), University of Tokyo (1950–1959), and Komazawa University (1959).

Kumja Paik Kim (born 1934) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She completed a doctorate at Stanford University and was appointed curator of Korean art at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco in 1989.

Kumkum Bandyopadhyay is an Indology and history/archaeology researcher. She studied under doctoral supervisor Rupendra Kumar Chattopadhyay and is attested as a Research Scholar or Fellow at the Asiatic Society in 2026.

Kun Chang (1917–2017) was a linguist, sinologist, and tibetologist. Educated at Tsinghua and Yale under Franklin Edgerton and Geshe Nornang, he held positions at Academia Sinica, the University of Washington (from 1951), and UC Berkeley (1963–1987).

Kunio Harikai (born 1942) is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Kyushu University under Seiren Matsunami and Shōren Ihara, and later served as an Associate Professor at Saga University (~1976–1993).
Kunio Iwaya (born 1943) studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1961 to 1969 and held a post at Meiji Gakuin University from ~1979 to 2014.
